final_message:
I've written the final parameters to `params.json`. With them, the image error against the reference photos dropped from about 5665 to 1133 (summed per-pixel squared error over all 12 photos). Measured by the mismatch of the cloth outline, the error fell from 5.24 to 1.72.

| parameter | start | final |
|---|---|---|
| stretch_stiffness | 100 N/m | **5000 N/m** |
| bend_stiffness | 100 N·m/rad | **0.005 N·m/rad** |
| areal_density | 1.0 kg/m² | **0.3 kg/m²** |
| friction | 0.5 | **0.85** |

**How I got there:** I scored each candidate by simulating both training episodes (center and corner), rendering the front and top cameras at 0.5, 1 and 2 s, and comparing them with the photos. I ran four batches of 12 candidates in parallel on the worker copies, then checked the chosen set against the photos by eye. The final values are an interpolation between the two best tested points, and I confirmed their score in the main app.

**What the photos pin down:**
- **Friction is the most clearly identified parameter.** The corner episode, where the cloth slides off the box edge, is very sensitive to it. At 0.3–0.65 the cloth slides off too far, and at 0.95–1.2 it sticks too much. The best score was at about 0.8–0.85, and 0.85 was best in the last batch.
- **Stretch stiffness is well identified in scale.** The default 100 N/m made the cloth sag like rubber, and 10⁵ N/m scored much worse everywhere. The best range was about 3×10³ to 10⁴ N/m.
- **Bending stiffness must be low.** The default 100 gave a stiff, board-like sheet, while the photos show fine wrinkles. Anywhere from 10⁻³ to 10⁻¹ scores about the same, so 0.005 is a reasonable value, not a precise one.
- **Areal density is only weakly identified.** Values from 0.1 to 0.6 scored within noise of each other. 0.3 is a middle value.

**Remaining mismatch:** in the center episode, the simulated cloth hangs slightly lower and flares out less at the corners than in the photos. Raising bending stiffness didn't fix this within the budget. The folds in the corner episode are chaotic, so their pixel-level differences can't be removed; the overall layout (how much of the box top stays covered, and where the pile lands on the floor) matches well at all three times.
